insights.tip0: Send invoices the same day you finish the job: they get paid up to twice as fast.
insights.tip1: Ask for a deposit (30–50%) on big jobs before buying materials.
insights.tip2: Set aside 25–30% of every payment for taxes in a separate account.
insights.tip3: Offer a maintenance plan (subscription): steady monthly income smooths slow seasons.
insights.tip4: Review your prices every 6 months; material costs change, your rates should too.
insights.tip5: Take before-and-after photos and attach them to the invoice: fewer disputes, faster payment.
insights.tip6: Keep 3 months of expenses as a cash cushion before expanding.
insights.tip7: Follow up on quotes within 48 hours; most customers decide in the first week.
insights.tip8: Track fuel and mileage per job to know which areas are really profitable.
insights.tip9: Offer card and Zelle payments: easier to pay means paid sooner.
insights.tip10: Bundle small add-ons (filters, inspections) into your main services.
insights.tip11: Call your best customers twice a year: repeat work costs nothing to win.
insights.tip12: Separate business and personal spending; it makes taxes and loans much easier.
insights.tip13: Check which service makes you the most profit, not just the most revenue.
insights.tip14: Late fees work best when they're written on the quote and invoice from day one.
insights.tip15: Buy materials per job, not 'just in case', to keep cash free.
insights.tip16: A Google review request right after payment can bring your next customer.
insights.tip17: Look at last year's same month to plan for slow and busy seasons.
insights.tip18: If one customer is more than 30% of your income, start diversifying.
insights.tip19: Write down why quotes are declined: price, timing or trust. Fix the most common one.
insights.lossT: You're spending more than you collect
insights.lossM: Start with the category that eats the most money and look for one cost you can pause this month.
insights.lossB: This year you've spent {spent} but collected {got}. Review your biggest expense categories and collect overdue invoices first.
insights.lowM: A small 5–10% price increase on your top services often lifts profit more than finding new customers.
insights.lowB: Service businesses usually aim for 20–40%. Consider raising prices on your most requested services or cutting one recurring cost.
insights.goodM: You're doing great. Move 25–30% of every payment to a separate account for taxes, and keep a cushion for slow months.
insights.goodB: You kept {amt} of every dollar collected this year. Set aside part of it for taxes and slow months.
insights.overM: Send the reminder by text or WhatsApp too: customers answer messages faster than emails.
insights.overB: {n, plural, one {# invoice is} other {# invoices are}} past due. A friendly reminder today usually gets paid within the week.
insights.upM: Good momentum. Ask today's happy customers for a Google review while the job is fresh.
insights.upB: You've received {now} this month vs {last} last month. Keep the momentum: follow up on open quotes.
insights.downM: Slow weeks are normal. Call past customers for maintenance work: it's the easiest job to win.
insights.downB: {now} so far this month vs {last} last month. The month isn't over: check unpaid invoices and quotes waiting for approval.
insights.spendM: Check if any of these purchases can be billed to a customer as materials.

insights.catB: Your biggest cost category. Compare suppliers or buy in bulk for the jobs you do most.
insights.quoteM: Quotes answered in the first 48 hours close much more often. A short follow-up text is enough.
